record.title: Weighted Berge–Fulkerson matching conjecture for bridgeless cubic graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a weighted bridgeless cubic graph, meaning that $G$ has no bridges, every vertex has degree $3$, and its edges have non-negative weights. Let $w(G)$ be the total edge weight and let $M$ be a **perfect matching**, a set of pairwise disjoint edges meeting every vertex exactly once.

**Weighted perfect-matching conjecture.** There exists a perfect matching $M$ such that

$$
w(M)\geq \frac{w(G)}{3}.
$$

This is presented as a weighted consequence of the Berge–Fulkerson conjecture and would imply the relevant case of the paper's triangle-free cubic bisection conjecture. Its general validity remains open.
record.source_name: Stefanie Gerke, Gregory Gutin, Anders Yeo and Yacong Zhou, “Lower Bounds for Maximum Weight Bisections of Graphs with Bounded Degrees”, arXiv:2401.10074 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.10074

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2024).

record.title: The center-realization conjecture for 2-connected plane graphs
record.statement: Let $H$ be a 2-connected plane graph. A vertex $v$ of $H$ is **quasi-eccentric to** $H[f]$ for a face $f$ of $H$ when the relevant quasi-eccentricity condition holds for the subgraph induced by the boundary of $f$. **Center-realization conjecture.** If each vertex of $H$ is quasi-eccentric to $H[f]$ for some face $f$ of $H$, then there exists a plane graph $G$ such that $H$ is both the center of $G$ and an isometric subgraph of $G$. The preceding results establish sharp order bounds for maximal planar graphs, but whether the analogous sufficient-and-necessary condition extends to this broader class of 2-connected plane graphs is left as a further question.
record.source_name: Brandon Du Preez, “Maximal planar graphs that embed as centers”, arXiv:2401.16831 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.16831

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2024).

record.title: The extremizer conjecture for the critical Riesz projection inequality
record.statement:
Let $1<q<2$ or $2<q\leq\infty$, let $\mathfrak{p}(q)$ be the one-dimensional critical exponent, and let $P_+$ denote the Riesz projection on the unit circle. **Extremizer conjecture.** If a nontrivial function $\psi\in L^q$ satisfies

$$
\|P_+\psi\|_{\mathfrak{p}(q)}=\|\psi\|_q,
$$

then there are a constant $C\neq0$ and an inner function $I$ such that $\psi=CI$. The endpoint $q=1$ is described as exceptional, and the asserted characterization is conjectured for the stated non-endpoint ranges.
record.source_name: Ole Fredrik Brevig, Adrián Llinares and Kristian Seip, “Critical exponents of the Riesz projection”, arXiv:2402.09787 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.09787

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2024).

record.title: Lower-bound conjecture for plane star-forest decompositions of complete geometric graphs
record.statement:
A **complete geometric graph** is a complete graph drawn with vertices in general position and straight-line edges. A **plane star-forest** is a forest whose connected components are stars. **Star-forest decomposition lower-bound conjecture.** Let $n\ge1$. There is no complete geometric graph with $n$ vertices that can be decomposed into fewer than

$$
\left\lceil\frac{3n}{4}\right\rceil
$$

plane star-forests.
The source presents this as a conjecture based on the lower bound known for vertices in convex position; its general case remains open.
record.source_name: Todor Antić, Jelena Glišić and Milan Milivojčević, “Star-Forest Decompositions of Complete Graphs”, arXiv:2402.11044 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.11044

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2024).

record.title: Tower-growth conjecture for hereditary 3-uniform hypergraph properties
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a hereditary property of $3$-uniform hypergraphs with infinite $\operatorname{VC}_2$-dimension. Let $L_{\mathcal{H}}(\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2)$ denote the associated regularity growth function, and let $Tw$ denote the tower function. **Tower-growth conjecture.** There exist a function $\epsilon_2:\mathbb{N}\rightarrow (0,1]$ and a constant $C>0$ such that

$$
L_{\mathcal{H}}(\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2)\geq Tw(\epsilon_1^{-C}).
$$

This conjecture proposes that the lower bound in the unbounded-$\operatorname{VC}_2$ range can be improved from exponential to at least tower growth; the paper suggests that techniques from its proof combined with bipartite lower-bound constructions for graph regularity may establish it. The source does not give evidence of a resolution.
record.source_name: C. Terry, “Growth of regular partitions 4: strong regularity and the pairs partition”, arXiv:2404.02030 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.02030

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2024).

record.title: Uniqueness conjecture for $(t,\lambda)$-liking digraphs
record.statement: Let $t\geq 3$ and let a **$(t,\lambda)$-liking digraph** be a digraph in which every set of $t$ vertices has exactly $\lambda$ common out-neighbors. A complete digraph is a digraph having an arc in each direction between every pair of distinct vertices. **Uniqueness conjecture.** The complete digraph on $t+\lambda$ vertices is the only $(t,\lambda)$-liking digraph. This would extend the corresponding result for $(t,\lambda)$-friendship graphs; the paper establishes the claim when $t\geq \lambda+2$, while the general case remains open.
record.source_name: Myungho Choi, Hojin Chu and Suh-Ryung Kim, “Digraphs in which every t vertices have exactly λ common out-neighbors”, arXiv:2405.02662 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.02662

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2024).

record.title: Figueroa-Centeno et al.'s product antimagic conjecture
record.statement: Let $G=(V,E)$ be a connected graph of size $m$. A labeling of its edges by $\{1,2,\dots,m\}$ is **product antimagic** if the products of the labels incident with the vertices are pairwise distinct. **Figueroa-Centeno et al.'s product antimagic conjecture.** Every connected graph of size at least three is product antimagic. Product antimagic labelings were introduced by Figueroa-Centeno et al.; the conjecture is presented as an open variation of the antimagic graph problem.
record.source_name: Mercè Mora and Joaquín Tey, “Antimagic and product antimagic graphs with pendant edges”, arXiv:2405.05375 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.05375

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2024). “This conjecture has received much attention (see ), but it is widely open in general.”

record.title: The (2,2)-Conjecture for graph decompositions
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph of order at least four. A **locally irregular multigraph** is a multigraph in which the endpoints of every edge have different degrees. For a subgraph $H$ of $G$, let ${}^2H$ denote the multigraph obtained by replacing each edge of $H$ by two parallel edges.

**(2,2)-Conjecture.** The graph $G$ can be decomposed into two subgraphs $G_1$ and $G_2$ such that there exist locally irregular multigraphs $M_1$ and $M_2$ satisfying

$$
G_1\subseteq M_1\subseteq {}^2G_1,
$$

$$
G_2\subseteq M_2\subseteq {}^2G_2.
$$

Equivalently, every connected graph of order at least four should have a $(2,2)$-coloring. This formulation connects locally irregular decompositions with neighbor-sum-distinguishing edge colorings; the source presents it as an open conjecture.
record.source_name: Igor Grzelec, Tomáš Madaras, Alfréd Onderko and Roman Soták, “On a new problem about the local irregularity of graphs”, arXiv:2405.13893 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.13893

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of May 2024).

record.title: Acyclic system conjecture via matching ensembles
record.statement: Let $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and $[d]=\{1,\ldots,d\}$. A **$k$-by-$k$ matching** is a matching between a $k$-subset of $[n]$ and a $k$-subset of $[d]$, and a **matching ensemble** is a collection of such matchings satisfying the matching-ensemble axioms. **Acyclic system conjecture using matching ensembles.** Suppose there is a collection of $2$-by-$2$ matchings between all $2$-subsets of $[n]$ and all $2$-subsets of $[3]$ satisfying the matching-ensemble axioms. Then one can add matchings between all $k$-subsets of $[n]$ and $[d]$ for $k=3,\dots,\min(n,d)$ so that the result is again a matching ensemble. The theorem immediately preceding this statement proves the $d=3$ extension through $3$-by-$3$ matchings; the general extension remains unresolved in the supplied text.
record.source_name: SuHo Oh, “Permutation ensembles on products of simplices”, arXiv:2504.21149 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.21149

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of April 2025). “As mentioned above, the above conjecture is false.”

record.title: Locally finite perturbation conjecture for edge-coloured complete graphs
record.statement: Let $k\ge2$ be an integer, let $K$ be a finite clique, and let $c$ be a $k$-colouring of the edges of $K$ such that there is an edge of every colour. A **locally finite perturbation** of an edge-colouring is a colouring obtained by changing colours on the edges of a nonempty locally finite subgraph. **Colouring perturbation conjecture.** There is a colouring $\chi$ of the edges of the complete countably infinite graph such that every locally finite perturbation contains a copy of $K$ with colouring $c$. This extends the locally finite perturbation question to coloured structures and remains open.
record.source_name: Marthe Bonamy, Carla Groenland, Tom Johnston, Natasha Morrison and Alex Scott, “Infinite induced-saturated graphs”, arXiv:2506.08810 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.08810

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2025).

record.title: The representation-number conjecture for larger toroidal grid graphs
record.statement:
Let $\text{TGr}_{m,n}$ be the toroidal grid graph formed from the Cartesian product of the cycle graphs $C_m$ and $C_n$, with $m,n\geq 3$, and let $\mathcal{R}(G)$ denote the representation number of a graph $G$. **Representation-number conjecture.** If $n,m\geq 3$ and $m+n\geq 8$, then

$$
\mathcal{R}(\text{TGr}_{m,n})\geq 4.
$$

The graphs $\text{TGr}_{3,3}$ and $\text{TGr}_{3,4}$ have known 3-representations, but no 3-representation is known for larger toroidal grid graphs; the conjecture predicts that all cases with $m+n\geq 8$ require representation number at least $4$.
record.source_name: Nawaf Shafi Alshammari, Sergey Kitaev and Artem Pyatkin, “On the representation number of grid graphs and cylindric grid graphs”, arXiv:2507.16469 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.16469

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2025).

record.title: The simple 2-connected cubic graph source-to-sink path-count conjecture
record.statement: Let $D$ be a simple, 2-connected, 3-regular acyclic directed graph on $2n$ vertices with a unique source and a unique sink. **Simple 2-connected path-count conjecture.** The graph $D$ has at most $(\sqrt{3})^n+1$ source-to-sink paths, and this bound is tight for even values of $n\geq2$. The proposed extremal family again uses repeated overlapping acyclic-triangle blocks together with an edge joining the source and sink to maintain connectivity; the bound and tightness assertion remain open.
record.source_name: François Clément and Dan Guyer, “Monotone Paths on Acyclic 3-Regular Graphs”, arXiv:2508.02108 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.02108

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2025).

record.title: The three-color majority-coloring conjecture for digraphs
record.statement: A **majority $k$-coloring** of a digraph $G$ is a vertex coloring $c:V(G)\rightarrow\{1,\ldots,k\}$ such that every vertex of color $i$ has at least as many out-neighbours of colors different from $i$ as it has out-neighbours of color $i$. **Three-color majority-coloring conjecture.** Every digraph has a majority coloring with $3$ colors. The result is known with $4$ colors, while the three-color case remains widely open, including for structured classes such as tournaments and Eulerian digraphs.
record.source_name: Jørgen Bang-Jensen, Francois Pirot and Anders Yeo, “Vertex-partitions of 2-edge-colored graphs”, arXiv:2508.18957 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.18957

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2025).

record.title: The 6-regular three-2-factor conjecture
record.statement: Let $G$ be a $6$-regular graph. A **2-factor** is a spanning $2$-regular subgraph, and a component of a $2$-factor is one of its connected components. **The 6-regular three-2-factor conjecture.** Every $6$-regular graph is decomposable into three $2$-factors, where one of these $2$-factors has a component with at least $4$ vertices. This is identified as a sufficient condition for the $6$-regular case of the paper's main open problem. The corresponding assertion for $8$-regular graphs follows from a theorem on non-isomorphic $2$-factors, but the stated $6$-regular conjecture remains unresolved in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Saieed Akbari, Jonny Aloni, Arash Beikmohammadi and Alexander Clow, “Tight Bounds for Cycle-Edge Decompositions and Covers”, arXiv:2509.01901 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.01901

Status: **open** according to the source (as of September 2025). “This old conjecture remains open, but some related results and special cases are known.”

record.title: Cycle-system extremal conjecture for glued-triangle graphs
record.statement:
For $n$ vertices, let $G_n$ be the connected graph obtained by gluing $n-2$ triangles along one common edge. **Cycle-system extremal conjecture.** The graph $G_n$ has exactly

$$
(n-1)^{(n-3)}
$$

cycle systems, and among all simple graphs with $n$ vertices, it has the maximal number of cycle systems. This is posed as a counting and extremal question about cycle systems of graphs; the supplied source gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Scott Corry, Anton Dochtermann, Solís McClain, David Perkinson and Lixing Yi, “Cycle systems, coparking functions, and h-vectors of matroids”, arXiv:2509.11460 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.11460

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2025).

record.title: Non-differentiability conjecture for dimensions of bounded-type Sturmian spectra
record.statement:
Let $\Sigma_{\alpha,\lambda}$ be the spectrum of the Sturmian Hamiltonian with frequency $\alpha$ and coupling constant $\lambda$. **Bounded-type non-differentiability conjecture.** There exists a frequency $\alpha$ of bounded type such that

$$
\lambda\mapsto\dim_H\Sigma_{\alpha,\lambda}
$$

is not differentiable at at least one point $\lambda_0$. This is proposed as a consequence of extending the paper's non-stationary hyperbolic argument beyond the quadratic irrational case; analytic dependence is known for quadratic irrational frequencies, while the corresponding almost-sure regularity is described as conjectural.
record.source_name: Victor Kleptsyn and Alexandro Luna, “On the Regularity of the Dimension of Cookie-Cutter-Like Sets”, arXiv:2511.07557 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.07557

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2025).

record.title: The local-to-global conjecture for acyclic dichromatic number
record.statement:
For a tournament $T$, let $N^+(v)$ be the out-neighborhood of $v$, and let $\vec{\chi}_{\rm a}(T)$ denote its acyclic dichromatic number.

**Local-to-global conjecture.** There exists a function $f\colon \mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ such that every tournament $T$ satisfies

$$
\vec{\chi}_{\rm a}(T)\leq\max_{v\in V(T)}f\bigl(\vec{\chi}_{\rm a}(T[N^+(v)])\bigr).
$$

The analogous statement for the ordinary dichromatic number is known. The acyclic version is proposed as a stronger local-to-global property and remains open.
record.source_name: Jørgen Bang-Jensen, Lucas Picasarri-Arrieta and Anders Yeo, “Acyclic dichromatic number of oriented graphs”, arXiv:2511.20246 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.20246

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2025). “The conjecture remains open for every $k\geq 2$.”

record.title: Partition concentration conjecture for powers of paths
record.statement:
Fix integers $k\geq2$ and $m\geq k+1$. Let $P$ be an $m$-path whose vertex set is partitioned as

$$
V(P)=V_1\cup\dots\cup V_{k+1}.
$$

For a vertex subset $V_j$, write $P[V_j]$ for the induced subgraph, and let $f(\ell_{k,m})$ be the quantity defined in the paper. **Partition concentration conjecture.** There exists a positive constant $c=c(m)$ such that some $j\in[k+1]$ satisfies

$$
|E(P[V_j])|\geq f(\ell_{k,m})|V_j|-c(m).
$$

This is proposed as a strengthening of a lemma that would confirm the preceding over-threshold conjecture. Its status is open in the source.
record.source_name: Sylwia Antoniuk, Andrzej Dudek and Andrzej Ruciński, “Powers of Hamiltonian cycles in randomly augmented Pósa-Seymour graphs”, arXiv:2512.23886 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.23886

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2025).

record.title: Wu–Xu–Xu conjecture on 3-colorability of even-hole-restricted graphs
record.statement:
For an integer $\ell\geq 2$, let ${\cal H}_{\ell}$ denote the family of graphs with girth $2\ell$ and no even holes of length at least $2\ell+2$.

**Wu–Xu–Xu conjecture.** Every graph in $\bigcup_{\ell\geq 2}{\cal H}_{\ell}$ is $3$-colorable.

This is the even-hole analogue of the resolved conjecture for the families ${\cal G}_{\ell}$. The source presents it as a proposed conjecture and gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Yan Wang and Rong Wu, “Graphs with girth 8 and without longer even holes are 3-colorable”, arXiv:2605.27943 (2026).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2025–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2509.01137](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.01137).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.27943

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of May 2026). “Plummer and Zha presented counterexamples to Robertson's conjecture, and conjectured that every pentagraph is $3$-colorable.”

record.title: The average-degree rainbow path conjecture for subgraphs of hypercubes
record.statement:
Let $Q_n$ be the $n$-dimensional hypercube, and let $G$ be a subgraph of $Q_n$. A proper edge-coloring of $G$ is one in which incident edges receive distinct colors, and a rainbow copy of a graph is a copy whose edges receive pairwise distinct colors.

**Average-degree rainbow path conjecture.** If $G$ has average degree at least $d$, then every proper edge-coloring of $G$ contains a rainbow copy of the path on $d$ edges.

This is an average-degree analogue of the Erdős–Sós conjecture and a rainbow conjecture proposed in the cited work. Even for subgraphs of hypercubes, the assertion remains open for $d\ge 5$.
record.source_name: Nicholas Crawford, Maya Sankar, Carl Schildkraut and Sam Spiro, “Rainbow Trees in Hypercubes”, arXiv:2508.14186 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.14186

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2025).
